metadata.title: Continuity of Operations (Secure‑Resilience Aligned)

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for maintaining essential functions during disruption when explicitly permitted by Secure‑Resilience.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Continuity planning, degraded operation modes, mission‑essential processes, and alternate execution paths.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Solution pattern implementing continuity operations subject to Secure‑Resilience eligibility and safety constraints.

props.name: secure-resilience-dependency
props.remarks: Continuity actions are governed by Secure‑Resilience state classification, recall status, and resume eligibility.

metadata.remarks: Continuity of Operations provides capability to maintain essential functions during disruption. Continuity does not imply full functionality, safety, or permission to resume normal operations.

components.title: Mission‑Essential Function Identification
components.description: Identification of functions permitted to continue during disruption.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Mission-essential functions are identified and prioritized.

components.title: Degraded Operation Modes
components.description: Explicitly defined reduced functionality modes permitted under continuity.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Alternate and degraded operational modes are supported.

components.title: Continuity Eligibility Gate
components.description: Permits continuity actions only when Secure‑Resilience determines they are safe.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Continuity arrangements are gated by safety and eligibility context.

components.title: Continuity Suppression
components.description: Suppresses continuity when recall, irreversible state, or safety constraints exist.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Alternate processing excludes unsafe components or operations.

components.title: Continuity Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what continuity capability does not grant or imply.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Continuity does not imply safety, correctness, or permission to operate normally.

tactics.name: Impact
tactics.description: Adversary actions intended to disrupt operations or availability.

categories.name: Degrade
categories.description: Operating systems with intentionally reduced capability.

categories.name: Alternate Processing
categories.description: Providing essential functions via alternate pathways.

categories.name: Isolate
categories.description: Preventing unsafe components from participating in continuity.
